alice: hey folks — seeing a p99 regression on FP8+INT4 mixed-precision paths with continuous batching after last runtime rollout. looks like the kernel selector flips to a slower generic path when padding_ratio > ~0.3 and there are KV cache hits. attaching quick profiler snippets and a repro command.

perf-bot: regression alert: service=inference-pool-3 metric=p99_latency before=110ms after=185ms deploy=2026-03-15-rt-v2 :warning:

ben: can you paste the repro command you used? i'll try on a dedicated slice.

alice: repro I used:
```bash
./tools/run_infer.sh \\  --model redwood/opt-6.7b-quant \\  --precision fp8,int4 \\  --batching continuous \\  --seq_dist "short:60%,mid:30%,long:10%" \\  --kv_cache true \\
```
Observed: p50 ~40ms (ok), p95 ~90ms, p99 jumps to 170-190ms.

carol: pasted the trimmed profiler flame:
```
[profiler] top frames
matmul_kernel_generic  48%
quant_dequant_copy    22%
kv_cache_read_copy    12%
padding_unpack        10%
other                 8%
```
Note that the selector chose `matmul_kernel_generic` instead of the fused `quant_conv_fast` for these shape combos. kernel shape shows width=37 which triggers pad->64 and causes heavy per-row work.

dave: hunch — the selector currently checks model_precision + seq_len and picks kernels, but treats any kv_cache_hit as 'full sequence' and forces a fallback -> that defeats fused quant path. we should compute `effective_active_tokens = total_tokens - kv_cached_tokens` and use that plus `padding_ratio = padded_tokens / effective_active_tokens` in the score. pseudocode: 
```py
score = base_score - alpha*padding_ratio - beta*(latency_est / batch_size)
if effective_active_tokens < token_threshold and padding_ratio < 0.35:
    prefer fused_quant_kernel
else:
    fallback generic
```

alice: tried forcing `force_kernel=fused_quant_fast` on the pool and reran — p99 dropped to ~115ms but p50/p95 got slightly worse (more variance) and token efficiency decreased ~6% (more quant ops). tradeoff but shows selector choice is root cause. :thumbsup:

carol: important: KV cache read currently does an extra memcpy into an aligned buffer before the fused kernel can use it. if selector assumes 'cache present => incompatible' we lose the optimized path. two fixes: (1) make fused kernels accept unaligned kv buffers (impl effort) or (2) let selector prefer fused kernel and insert small path to realign only when chosen. (2) is lower-risk.

ben: i'll run a small A/B on dedicated pool-7. can you drop the exact trace id or s3 path? i'll collect perf counters (L2 miss, memcpy bytes, kernel_choice).

alice: trace uploaded -> s3://redwood-traces/rt/1769991001/trace-compact.json. key bits: `padding_ratio=0.42`, `kv_cache_hit_rate=0.28`, `kernel_selected=matmul_kernel_generic`.

carol: another observation from the trace: calibration step for FP8 moved some weights into a different quant block size, which changed matrix dims slightly and pushed several GEMM shapes into the pathological odd-width region. calibration improved accuracy but unintentionally made kernel shapes worse. we should add a calibration check that warns when resulting tile shapes increase padding_ratio > 0.25 for common seq distributions.

dave: agreed. plan proposal: 1) change selector to account for effective_active_tokens and padding_ratio (small PR), 2) add a `calib-shape-check` post-calib job that emits a flag for runtime to prefer different quant blockings, 3) short-term allow forced `fused_quant_fast` override for affected customers. i'll draft PR.

ben: sounds good. i'll run tests on pool-7 and report counters. tagging @carol for kernel impl notes.

alice: thanks — opening an issue with links and steps: https://git.internal/redwood/issues/INF-4621 (will add perf snapshots).

perf-bot: note: marking this thread linked to INF-4621 and regression alert cleared when manual override applied. :white_check_mark:
